33. And his father and mother were wondering about those things which were spoken of him. 34. And Simeon blessed them, and said to Mary his mother, Lo, this (child) has been set for the ruin, and for the resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign, which is spoken against. 35. But also a sword shall pierce thy own soul: that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed. 36. And there was Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher: she had advanced to a great age, and had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity. 37. And she was a widow of about eighty-four years, who departed not from the temple worshipping (God) with fastings and prayer day and night. 38. And she, coming in at that hour, made acknowledgments also to God, [199] and spake of him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem. 39. And when they had completed all things according to the Law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own city Nazareth.

33. And his father and mother were wondering Luke does not say, that they were astonished at it as a new thing, but that they contemplated with reverence, and embraced with becoming admiration, this prediction of the Spirit uttered by the lips of Simeon, so that they continued to make progress in the knowledge of Christ. We learn from this example that, when we have once come to possess a right faith, we ought to collect, on every hand, whatever may aid in giving to it additional strength. That man has made great proficiency in the word of God, who does not fail to admire whatever he reads or hears every day, that contributes to his unceasing progress in faith.

34. And Simeon blessed them If you confine this to Joseph and Mary, there will be no difficulty. But, as Luke appears to include Christ at the same time, it might be asked, What right had Simeon to take upon him the office of blessing Christ? "Without all contradiction," says Paul, "the less is blessed of the greater," (Hebrews 7:7.) Besides, it has the appearance of absurdity, that any mortal man should offer prayers in behalf of the Son of God. I:answer: The Apostle does not speak there of every kind of blessing, but only of the priestly blessing: for, in other respects, it is highly proper in men to pray for each other. Now, it is more probable that Simeon blessed them, as a private man and as one of the people, than that he did so in a public character: for, as we have already said, we nowhere read that he was a priest. But there would be no absurdity in saying, that he prayed for the prosperity and advancement of Christ's kingdom: for in the book of Psalms the Spirit prescribes such a eulogia,--a blessing of this nature to all the godly.

"Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; we have blessed you in the name of the Lords"
(Psalm 118:26.)

Lo, this has been set This discourse was, no doubt, directly addressed by Simeon to Mary; but it has a general reference to all the godly. The holy virgin needed this admonition, that she might not (as usually happens) be lifted up by prosperous beginnings, so as to be less prepared for enduring afflictive events. But she needed it on another account, that she might not expect Christ to be received by the people with universal applause, but that her mind, on the contrary, might be fortified by unshaken courage against all hostile attacks. It was the design, at the same time, of the Spirit of God, to lay down a general instruction for all the godly. When they see the world opposing Christ with wicked obstinacy, they must be prepared to meet that opposition, and to contend against it undismayed. The unbelief of the world is--we know it--a great and serious hinderance; but it must be conquered, if we wish to believe in Christ. There never was a state of human society so happily constituted, that the greater part followed Christ. Those who will enlist in the cause of Christ must learn this as one of their earliest lessons, and must "put on" this "armor," (Ephesians 6:11,) that they may be steadfast in believing on him.

It was by far the heaviest temptation, that Christ was not acknowledged by his own countrymen, and was even ignominiously rejected by that nation, which boasted that it was the Church of God; and, particularly, that the priests and scribes, who held in their hands the government of the Church, were his most determined enemies. For who would have thought, that he was the King of those, who not only rejected him, but treated him with such contempt and outrage?

We see, then, that a good purpose was served by Simeon's prediction, that Christ was set for the ruin of many in Israel The meaning is, that he was divinely appointed to cast down and destroy many. But it must be observed, that the ruin of unbelievers results from their striking against him. This is immediately afterwards expressed, when Simeon says that Christ is a sign, which is spoken against Because unbelievers are rebels against Christ, they clash themselves against him, and hence comes their ruin This metaphor is taken from a mark shot at by archers, [200] as if Simeon had said, Hence we perceive the malice of men, and even the depravity of the whole human race, that all, as if they had made a conspiracy, rise in murmurs and rebellion against the Son of God. The world would not display such harmony in opposing the Gospel, if there were not a natural enmity between the Son of God and those men. The ambition or fury of the enemies of the Gospel carries them in various directions, faction splits them into various sects, and a wide variety of superstitions distinguishes idolaters from each other. But while they thus differ among themselves, they all agree in this, to oppose the Son of God. It has been justly observed, that the opposition everywhere made to Christ is too plain an evidence of human depravity. That the world should thus rise against its Creator is a monstrous sight. But Scripture predicted that this would happen, and the reason is very apparent, that men who have once been alienated from God by sin, always fly from him. Instances of this kind, therefore, ought not to take us by surprise; but, on the contrary, our faith, provided with this armor, ought to be prepared to fight with the contradiction of the world.

As God has now gathered an Israel to himself from the whole world, and there is no longer a distinction between the Jew and the Greek, the same thing must now happen as, we learn, happened before. Isaiah had said of his own age,

"The Lord will be for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offense, to both the houses of Israel," (Isaiah 8:14.)

From that time, the Jews hardly ever ceased to dash themselves against God, but the rudest shock was against Christ. The same madness is now imitated by those who call themselves Christians; and even those, who lay haughty claims to the first rank in the Church, frequently employ all the power which they possess in oppressing Christ. But let us remember, all that they gain is, to be at length crushed and "broken in pieces," (Isaiah 8:9.)

Under the word ruin the Spirit denounces the punishment of unbelievers, and thus warns us to keep at the greatest possible distance from them; lest, by associating with them, we become involved in the same destruction. And Christ is not the less worthy of esteem, because, when he appears, many are ruined: for the "savor" of the Gospel is not less "sweet" and delightful to God, (2 Corinthians 2:15,16,) though it is destructive to the ungodly world. Does any one inquire, how Christ occasions the ruin of unbelievers, who without him were already lost? The reply is easy. Those who voluntarily deprive themselves of the salvation which God has offered to them, perish twice. Ruin implies the double punishment which awaits all unbelievers, after that they have knowingly and wilfully opposed the Son of God.

And for the resurrection This consolation is presented as a contrast with the former clause, to make it less painful to our feelings: for, if nothing else were added, it would be melancholy to hear, that Christ is "a stone of stumbling," which will break and crush, by its hardness, a great part of men. Scripture therefore reminds us of his office, which is entirely different: for the salvation of men, which is founded on it, is secure; as Isaiah also says, "Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread; and he shall be for a sanctuary," or fortress of defense, (Isaiah 8:13,14.) And Peter speaks more clearly:

"To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God and precious, ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house. Wherefore also it is contained in Scripture, Behold, I lay in Zion the head-stone of the corner, elect, precious, and he that believeth in him shall not be confounded. Unto you, therefore, which believe, he is precious: but unto them who are disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner," (1 Peter 2:4-7; Isaiah 28:16.)

That we may not be terrified by the designation bestowed on Christ, "a stone of stumbling," let it be instantly recollected, on the other hand, that he is likewise called the "corner-stone," on which rests the salvation of all the godly. [201]

Let it be also taken into account, that the former is accidental, while the latter is properly and strictly his office. Besides, it deserves our notice, that Christ is not only called the support, but the resurrection of the godly: for the condition of men is not one in which it is safe for them to remain. They must rise from death, before they begin to live.

35. But also a sword shall pierce thy own soul This warning must have contributed greatly to fortify the mind of the holy virgin, and to prevent her from being overwhelmed with grief, when she came to those distressing struggles, which she had to undergo. Though her faith was agitated and tormented by various temptations, yet her sorest battle was with the cross: for Christ might appear to be utterly destroyed. She was not overwhelmed with grief; but it would have required a heart of stone not to be deeply wounded: for the patience of the saints differs widely from stupidity.

That the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed There are some who connect this clause with a part of the former verse, that Christ is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many in Israel; and who include in a parenthesis what we have just now explained about the sword: but it is better, I think, to refer it to the whole passage. The particle that, hopos an, in this passage, does not strictly denote a cause, but merely a consequence. When the light of the Gospel arises, and persecutions immediately spring up, there is, at the same time, a disclosure of affections of the heart, which had been hitherto concealed: for the lurking-places of human dissimulation are so deep, that they easily remain hidden till Christ comes. [202] But Christ, by his light, discloses every artifice, and unmasks hypocrisy; and to him is properly ascribed the office of laying open the secrets of the heart. But when the cross is added to doctrine it tries the hearts more to the quick. For those who have embraced Christ by outward profession, often shrink from bearing the cross, and, when they see the Church exposed to numerous calamities, easily desert their post.

36. And there was Anna, a prophetess Luke mentions not more than two persons who received Christ; and this is intended to teach us, that whatever belongs to God, however small it may be, ought to be preferred by us to the whole world. The scribes and priests, no doubt, were then surrounded by great splendor; but, as the Spirit of God, whose presence was not at all enjoyed by those rulers, [203] dwelt in Simeon and Anna, those two persons are entitled to greater reverence than an immense multitude of those whose pride is swelled by nothing but empty titles. For this reason, the historian mentions Anna's age, gives her the designation of prophetess, and, thirdly, bears a remarkable testimony to her piety, and to the holiness and chastity of her life. These are the qualities that justly give to men weight and estimation. And certainly none are led astray by the dazzling and empty magnificence of outward show, but those who are drawn, by the vanity of their own minds, to take pleasure in being deceived.

She had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity This is intended to inform us, that she was a widow in the very prime of life. She had married young, and shortly afterwards lost her husband; and the circumstance of her not entering into a second marriage while she was in the rigor of her bodily frame, [204] is mentioned with the view of heightening the commendation of her chastity. What follows, that she was a widow of about eighty-four years, may be explained in two ways. Either that time had passed in her unmarried state, [205] or it was the whole period of her life. If you reckon the eighty-four years as the time of her widowhood, it will follow that she was more than a hundred years old: but I leave that matter doubtful. The Spirit of prophecy still shone in a very few, who served as tokens to attest the doctrine of the Law and the Jewish religion, till the coming of Christ. In a state of society so dissolute, the elect of God needed such aids to prevent them from being carried away.

37. She departed not from the temple This is a hyperbolical expression; but the meaning is plain, that Anna was almost constantly in the temple. Luke adds, that she worshipped God with fastings and prayers day and night Hence we infer, that she did not visit the temple for the mere purpose of performing the outward service, but that she added to it the other exercises of piety. It deserves our attention, that the same rule is not enjoined on all, and that all ought not to be led indiscriminately to copy those performances, which are here commended in a widow. Each person ought to make a judicious inquiry, what belongs to his own calling. Silly ambition has filled the world with apes, from superstitious persons seizing, with more "zeal" than "knowledges" (Romans 10:2,) every thing that they hear praised in the saints: as if the distinction of rank did not render a selection of employments necessary, that each person may answer to his own calling. What is here related of Anna, Paul applies in a particular manner to widows, (1 Timothy 5:5;) so that married people act a foolish part, if they regulate their life by an unsuitable model.

But there still remains another doubt. Luke appears to make fastings a part of divine worship But we must observe, that of the acts which relate to worship, some are simply required, and, as we are accustomed to say, are in themselves necessary; while others are accessory, and have no other design than to aid the former class. Prayers belong strictly to the worship of God. Fasting is a subordinate aid, which is pleasing to God no farther than as it aids the earnestness and fervency of prayer. We must hold by this rule, that the duties of men are to be judged according as they are directed to a proper and lawful end. We must hold, also, by this distinction, that prayers are a direct worship of God; while fastings are a part of worship only on account of their consequences. Nor is there any reason to doubt, that the holy woman employed fastings as an excitement to bewail those calamities of the Church which then existed.

38. Made acknowledgment also to God [206] The holy melody, which proceeded from the lips of Simeon and Anna, is praised by Luke, in order that believers may exhort each other to sing with one mouth the praises of God, and may give mutual replies. When he says, that Anna spake of him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem, he again points out the small number of the godly. For the substance of faith lay in this expectation; and it is evident, that there were few who actually cherished it in their minds.

39. They returned to Galilee The departure to Egypt, I readily acknowledge, came between those events; and the fact mentioned by Luke, that they dwelt in their own city Nazareth, is later, in point of time, than the flight into Egypt, which Matthew relates, (Matthew 2:14.) But if there was no impropriety in one Evangelist leaving out what is related by another, there was nothing to prevent Luke from overleaping the period which he did not intend to mention, and passing at once to the following history. I am very far from agreeing with those who imagine that Joseph and Mary, after having finished the sacrifice of purification, returned to Bethlehem, to live there. Those persons are foolish enough to believe, that Joseph had a settled abode in a place where he was so little known, that he was unable to find a temporary lodging. Nor is it without a good reason that Luke says, with respect both to Joseph and Mary, that Nazareth was their own city We infer from it, that he never was an inhabitant of Bethlehem, though it was the place of his extraction. [207] As to the order of time, I shall presently give a more full explanation.

Footnotes:

[201] "La maitresse Pierre du coin, sur laquelle est fonde le salut de tous les enfans de Dieu." -- "The head-stone of the corner, on which is founded the salvation of all the children of God."

b98.es:
33. Y su padre y su madre estaban maravillados de las cosas que se decían de él. 34. Y Simeón los bendijo, y dijo a María su madre: He aquí, éste ha sido puesto para ruina y para resurrección de muchos en Israel, y para señal de que se habla en contra. 35. Pero también una espada traspasará tu propia alma, para que sean revelados los pensamientos de muchos corazones. 36. Y estaba allí Ana, profetisa, hija de Fanuel, de la tribu de Aser: había llegado a una edad avanzada, y había vivido con su marido siete años desde su virginidad. 37. Y ella era viuda como de ochenta y cuatro años, y no se apartaba del templo adorando (a Dios) con ayunos y oración día y noche. 38. Y ella, entrando en aquella hora, dio también gracias a Dios, [199] y habló de él a todos los que esperaban la redención en Jerusalén. 39. Y cuando hubieron cumplido todo según la Ley del Señor, regresaron a Galilea, a su ciudad de Nazaret.

33. Y su padre y su madre estaban maravillados. Lucas no dice que se asombraran de esto como algo nuevo, sino que contemplaron con reverencia y abrazaron con debida admiración esta predicción del Espíritu pronunciada por los labios de Simeón, de modo que continuaron progresando en el conocimiento de Cristo. De este ejemplo aprendemos que, una vez que hemos llegado a poseer una fe correcta, debemos recolectar, de todas partes, todo lo que pueda ayudar a darle fuerza adicional. Ha adquirido gran dominio de la palabra de Dios aquel hombre que no deja de admirar todo lo que lee u oye cada día, lo que contribuye a su incesante progreso en la fe.

34. Y Simeón los bendijo. Si limitas esto a José y María, no habrá dificultad. Pero, como Lucas parece incluir a Cristo al mismo tiempo, podría preguntarse: ¿Qué derecho tenía Simeón a asumir el oficio de bendecir a Cristo? "Sin contradicción alguna", dice Pablo, "lo menos es bendecido por lo mayor" (Hebreos 7:7). Además, tiene la apariencia de absurdo que cualquier hombre mortal ofrezca oraciones en nombre del Hijo de Dios. Respondo: El Apóstol no habla allí de toda clase de bendiciones, sino sólo de la bendición sacerdotal; porque, en lo demás, es muy apropiado que los hombres oren unos por otros. Ahora bien, es más probable que Simeón los bendijera, como hombre privado y como uno del pueblo, que lo hiciera en carácter público: porque, como ya hemos dicho, en ninguna parte leemos que fuera sacerdote. Pero no sería absurdo decir que oró por la prosperidad y el avance del reino de Cristo: porque en el libro de los Salmos el Espíritu prescribe tal elogia, una bendición de esta naturaleza para todos los piadosos.

"Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor; en el nombre de los Señores os hemos bendecido"
(Salmo 118:26.)

He aquí, esto ha sido establecido. Este discurso, sin duda, fue dirigido directamente por Simeón a María; pero tiene una referencia general a todos los piadosos. La santa virgen necesitaba esta amonestación, para que (como suele suceder) no se enalteciera con comienzos prósperos, de modo que estuviera menos preparada para soportar acontecimientos aflictivos. Pero lo necesitaba por otra razón, para no esperar que Cristo fuera recibido por el pueblo con aplauso universal, sino para que su mente, por el contrario, se fortaleciera con un coraje inquebrantable contra todos los ataques hostiles. Fue el designio, al mismo tiempo, del Espíritu de Dios, establecer una instrucción general para todos los piadosos. Cuando ven que el mundo se opone a Cristo con perversa obstinación, deben estar preparados para enfrentar esa oposición y luchar contra ella sin desmayarse. La incredulidad del mundo es, lo sabemos, un obstáculo grande y grave; pero debemos conquistarlo si queremos creer en Cristo. Nunca hubo un estado de la sociedad humana tan felizmente constituido, que la mayor parte siguiera a Cristo. Aquellos que se alistarán en la causa de Cristo deben aprender esto como una de sus primeras lecciones y deben "ponerse" esta "armadura" (Efesios 6:11) para ser firmes en creer en él.

Fue, con mucho, la tentación más grave, que Cristo no fuera reconocido por sus propios compatriotas, e incluso fue rechazado ignominiosamente por esa nación, que se jactaba de ser la Iglesia de Dios; y, particularmente, que los sacerdotes y escribas, que tenían en sus manos el gobierno de la Iglesia, eran sus enemigos más decididos. ¿Quién hubiera pensado que él era el Rey de aquellos que no sólo lo rechazaron, sino que lo trataron con tanto desprecio e indignación?

Vemos, entonces, que la predicción de Simeón cumplió un buen propósito: que Cristo estaba destinado a la ruina de muchos en Israel. El significado es que fue divinamente designado para derribar y destruir a muchos. Pero debe observarse que la ruina de los incrédulos resulta de su ataque contra él. Esto se expresa inmediatamente después, cuando Simeón dice que Cristo es un signo del que se habla en contra. Porque los incrédulos son rebeldes contra Cristo, chocan contra él, y de ahí viene su ruina. Esta metáfora está tomada de una diana disparada por los arqueros, [200] como si Simeón hubiera dicho: De aquí percibimos la malicia de los hombres, e incluso la depravación de todo el género humano, que todos, como si hubieran conspirado, se levantan en murmullos y rebeliones contra el Hijo de Dios. El mundo no mostraría tal armonía al oponerse al Evangelio, si no hubiera una enemistad natural entre el Hijo de Dios y esos hombres. La ambición o la furia de los enemigos del Evangelio los lleva en diversas direcciones, las facciones los dividen en varias sectas y una amplia variedad de supersticiones distingue a los idólatras entre sí. Pero aunque difieren entre sí, todos coinciden en oponerse al Hijo de Dios. Se ha observado con razón que la oposición que en todas partes se hace a Cristo es una evidencia demasiado clara de la depravación humana. Que el mundo se levante así contra su Creador es un espectáculo monstruoso. Pero las Escrituras predijeron que esto sucedería, y la razón es muy evidente: los hombres que una vez han sido alejados de Dios por el pecado, siempre huyen de él. Por lo tanto, casos de este tipo no deberían tomarnos por sorpresa; pero, por el contrario, nuestra fe, provista de esta armadura, debe estar preparada para luchar contra la contradicción del mundo.

Como Dios ahora ha reunido para sí a un Israel de todo el mundo, y ya no hay distinción entre judíos y griegos, ahora debe suceder lo mismo que, según sabemos, sucedió antes. Isaías había dicho de su propia época:

"El Señor será por piedra de tropiezo y por roca de escándalo para ambas casas de Israel" (Isaías 8:14).

Desde entonces, los judíos casi nunca dejaron de lanzarse contra Dios, pero el choque más duro fue contra Cristo. La misma locura ahora la imitan quienes se dicen cristianos; e incluso aquellos que pretenden altivamente el primer rango en la Iglesia, frecuentemente emplean todo el poder que poseen para oprimir a Cristo. Pero recordemos que todo lo que ganan es ser finalmente aplastados y "rotos en pedazos" (Isaías 8:9).

Bajo la palabra ruina, el Espíritu denuncia el castigo de los incrédulos y, por lo tanto, nos advierte que nos mantengamos a la mayor distancia posible de ellos; no sea que, al asociarnos con ellos, quedemos envueltos en la misma destrucción. Y Cristo no es menos digno de estima porque, cuando aparece, muchos quedan arruinados: porque el "olor" del Evangelio no es menos "dulce" y deleitable para Dios (2 Corintios 2:15,16), aunque es destructivo para el mundo impío. ¿Alguien pregunta cómo Cristo ocasiona la ruina de los incrédulos, que sin él ya estaban perdidos? La respuesta es fácil. Quienes se privan voluntariamente de la salvación que Dios les ha ofrecido, perecen dos veces. La ruina implica el doble castigo que espera a todos los incrédulos, después de que se han opuesto consciente y voluntariamente al Hijo de Dios.

Y para la resurrección Este consuelo se presenta en contraste con la cláusula anterior, para hacerlo menos doloroso para nuestros sentimientos: porque, si no se agregara nada más, sería melancólico escuchar que Cristo es "una piedra de tropiezo", que quebrantará y aplastará, por su dureza, a gran parte de los hombres. Por tanto, la Escritura nos recuerda su oficio, que es completamente diferente: porque la salvación de los hombres, que se basa en él, es segura; como también dice Isaías: "Santificad al Señor de los ejércitos mismo; y él sea vuestro temor, y él sea vuestro temor; y él será por santuario", o fortaleza de defensa, (Isaías 8:13,14.) Y Pedro habla más claramente:

"Acercándose a los cuales, como piedra viva, desechada ciertamente por los hombres, pero escogida por Dios y preciosa, vosotros también, como piedras vivas, sed edificados como casa espiritual. Por lo cual también está contenido en la Escritura: He aquí, yo pongo en Sion la piedra angular del ángulo, escogida, preciosa, y el que en ella cree no será confundido. Por tanto, para vosotros los que creéis, él es preciosa; pero para los desobedientes, la piedra que los constructores rechazado, éste se convierte en cabeza del ángulo" (1 Pedro 2:4-7; Isaías 28:16.)

Para que no nos aterrorice la designación otorgada a Cristo, "piedra de tropiezo", recordemos al instante, por otra parte, que también se le llama la "piedra angular", sobre la cual descansa la salvación de todos los piadosos. [201]

Tengamos también en cuenta que lo primero es accidental, mientras que lo segundo es propia y estrictamente su oficio. Además, merece nuestra atención que a Cristo no sólo se le llama apoyo, sino también resurrección de los piadosos: porque la condición de los hombres no es una en la que les sea seguro permanecer. Deben resucitar de la muerte antes de comenzar a vivir.

35. Pero también una espada traspasará tu propia alma. Esta advertencia debió contribuir en gran medida a fortalecer la mente de la santa virgen, y a evitar que se abrumara de dolor, cuando llegó a aquellas angustiosas luchas que tuvo que pasar. Aunque su fe estaba agitada y atormentada por varias tentaciones, su batalla más dolorosa fue con la cruz: porque Cristo podría parecer completamente destruido. Ella no estaba abrumada por el dolor; pero habría sido necesario un corazón de piedra para no quedar profundamente herido: porque la paciencia de los santos difiere mucho de la estupidez.

Para que sean revelados los pensamientos de muchos corazones. Hay algunos que conectan esta cláusula con una parte del versículo anterior, que Cristo está destinado a la ruina y la resurrección de muchos en Israel; y que incluyen entre paréntesis lo que acabamos de explicar sobre la espada: pero creo que es mejor referirlo a todo el pasaje. La partícula que, hopos an, en este pasaje, no denota estrictamente una causa, sino simplemente una consecuencia. Cuando surge la luz del Evangelio, e inmediatamente surgen las persecuciones, hay, al mismo tiempo, una revelación de los afectos del corazón, que hasta ahora habían estado ocultos: porque los escondites del disimulo humano son tan profundos que fácilmente permanecen ocultos hasta que venga Cristo. [202] Pero Cristo, con su luz, revela todo artificio y desenmascara la hipocresía; ya él se le atribuye apropiadamente el oficio de revelar los secretos del corazón. Pero cuando se añade la cruz a la doctrina, prueba más los corazones. Porque aquellos que han abrazado a Cristo por profesión exterior, a menudo evitan llevar la cruz y, cuando ven a la Iglesia expuesta a numerosas calamidades, fácilmente abandonan su puesto.

36. Y estaba Ana, una profetisa. Lucas menciona no más de dos personas que recibieron a Cristo; y esto tiene como objetivo enseñarnos que todo lo que pertenece a Dios, por pequeño que sea, debemos preferirlo al mundo entero. Los escribas y sacerdotes, sin duda, estuvieron entonces rodeados de gran esplendor; pero, como el Espíritu de Dios, cuya presencia no disfrutaban en absoluto esos gobernantes, [203] habitaba en Simeón y Ana, esas dos personas tienen derecho a mayor reverencia que una inmensa multitud de aquellos cuyo orgullo no está hinchado más que por títulos vacíos. Por esta razón, el historiador menciona la edad de Ana, le da el título de profetisa y, en tercer lugar, da un testimonio notable de su piedad y de la santidad y castidad de su vida. Éstas son las cualidades que justamente dan peso y estimación a los hombres. Y ciertamente nadie se desvía por la magnificencia deslumbrante y vacía de la apariencia exterior, sino aquellos que, por la vanidad de sus propias mentes, se sienten atraídos por el placer de ser engañados.

Había vivido con su marido siete años desde su virginidad. Esto pretende informarnos que era viuda en la flor de la vida. Se casó joven y poco después perdió a su marido; y la circunstancia de que ella no contrajo un segundo matrimonio mientras estaba en el rigor de su estructura corporal, [204] se menciona con el fin de realzar el elogio de su castidad. Lo que sigue, que ella era viuda durante unos ochenta y cuatro años, puede explicarse de dos maneras. O ese tiempo había transcurrido en su estado de soltería, [205] o era todo el período de su vida. Si se cuentan los ochenta y cuatro años como el tiempo de su viudez, se deduce que tenía más de cien años: pero dejo esa cuestión en duda. El Espíritu de profecía aún brillaba en muy pocos, que sirvieron de señales para dar fe de la doctrina de la Ley y de la religión judía, hasta la venida de Cristo. En un estado de sociedad tan disoluto, los elegidos de Dios necesitaban tales ayudas para evitar que se dejaran llevar.

37. Ella no se apartó del templo. Esta es una expresión hiperbólica; pero el significado es claro: Anna estaba casi constantemente en el templo. Lucas agrega que ella adoraba a Dios con ayunos y oraciones día y noche. De ahí inferimos que ella no visitó el templo con el mero propósito de realizar el servicio externo, sino que agregó otros ejercicios de piedad. Merece nuestra atención que no se impone la misma regla a todos, y que no todos deben ser inducidos indiscriminadamente a copiar aquellas actuaciones que aquí se recomiendan en una viuda. Cada uno debe hacer una investigación juiciosa sobre lo que pertenece a su propia vocación. La tonta ambición ha llenado el mundo de simios, de personas supersticiosas que se apoderan, con más "celo" que "conocimientos" (Romanos 10:2), de todo lo que escuchan alabado en los santos: como si la distinción de rango no hiciera necesaria una selección de empleos, para que cada persona pueda responder a su propia vocación. Lo que aquí se relata de Anna, Pablo lo aplica de manera particular a las viudas (1 Timoteo 5:5;) de modo que las personas casadas actúen como una tontería, si regulan su vida según un modelo inadecuado.

Pero aún queda otra duda. Lucas parece hacer que los ayunos sean parte del culto divino. Pero debemos observar que, de los actos que se relacionan con el culto, algunos son simplemente requeridos y, como estamos acostumbrados a decir, son en sí mismos necesarios; mientras que otros son accesorios y no tienen otro propósito que ayudar a la primera clase. Las oraciones pertenecen estrictamente a la adoración de Dios. El ayuno es una ayuda subordinada, que agrada a Dios sólo porque ayuda a la seriedad y el fervor de la oración. Debemos sostener, según esta regla, que los deberes de los hombres deben juzgarse según estén dirigidos a un fin adecuado y legítimo. Debemos sostener, también, por esta distinción, que las oraciones son una adoración directa a Dios; mientras que los ayunos son parte del culto sólo por sus consecuencias. Tampoco hay razón para dudar de que la santa mujer empleaba los ayunos como un estímulo para lamentar las calamidades de la Iglesia que entonces existían.

38. También hizo reconocimiento a Dios [206] La santa melodía, que salió de los labios de Simeón y Ana, es alabada por Lucas, para que los creyentes puedan exhortarse unos a otros a cantar con una sola boca las alabanzas de Dios, y puedan darse respuestas mutuas. Cuando dice que Ana habló de él a todos los que esperaban la redención en Jerusalén, nuevamente señala el pequeño número de los piadosos. Porque la sustancia de la fe residía en esta expectativa; y es evidente que fueron pocos los que realmente lo guardaron en sus mentes.

39. Regresaron a Galilea. Reconozco fácilmente que la partida a Egipto se produjo entre esos acontecimientos; y el hecho mencionado por Lucas, de que habitaban en su propia ciudad, Nazaret, es posterior, en el tiempo, a la huida a Egipto, que relata Mateo (Mateo 2:14). Pero si no hubo incorrección en que un evangelista omitiera lo que relata otro, no hubo nada que impidiera que Lucas se saltara el período que no tenía intención de mencionar y pasara de inmediato a la siguiente historia. Estoy muy lejos de estar de acuerdo con quienes imaginan que José y María, después de haber terminado el sacrificio de la purificación, regresaron a Belén para vivir allí. Esas personas son lo suficientemente tontas como para creer que José tenía una morada establecida en un lugar donde era tan poco conocido, que no pudo encontrar un alojamiento temporal. Tampoco es sin una buena razón que Lucas dice, con respecto tanto a José como a María, que Nazaret era su propia ciudad. De ello inferimos que nunca fue un habitante de Belén, aunque fue el lugar de su extracción. [207] En cuanto al orden del tiempo, daré a continuación una explicación más completa.

Notas a pie de página:

[199] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur"; -- "alabado también al Señor".

[200] "Ceste facon de parler contient une metaphore prise des arbalestiers, ou autres qui visent au blanc". -- "Esta forma de hablar contiene una metáfora, tomada de los arqueros u otros que apuntan a una marca".

[201] "La maitresse Pierre du coin, sur laquelle est fonde le salut de tous les enfans de Dieu". -- "La piedra angular del ángulo, sobre la cual se fundamenta la salvación de todos los hijos de Dios".

[202] "Extra Cristo"; -- "jusqu'a ce que Jesucristo viene".

[203] La palabra gobernantes (príncipes) parece usarse aquí con sarcasmo; porque su propia traducción es "duquel estoyment du tout destituez les autres, combien que ce fussent les gouverneurs"; - "de los cuales los demás estaban completamente desprovistos, aunque eran gobernantes".

[204] "Quum adhuc vegeto esset corpore".

[205] "Il y avoit tan de temps que son mari estoit mort"; -- "hacía tanto tiempo que su marido había muerto."

[206] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur"; -- "alabado también al Señor".

[207] "Combien que ce fust le pays de ses ancestres"; -- "aunque era el país de sus antepasados".

b99.en:
34. And Simeon blessed them If you confine this to Joseph and Mary, there will be no difficulty. But, as Luke appears to include Christ at the same time, it might be asked, What right had Simeon to take upon him the office of blessing Christ? "Without all contradiction," says Paul, "the less is blessed of the greater," (Hebrews 7:7.) Besides, it has the appearance of absurdity, that any mortal man should offer prayers in behalf of the Son of God. I:answer: The Apostle does not speak there of every kind of blessing, but only of the priestly blessing: for, in other respects, it is highly proper in men to pray for each other. Now, it is more probable that Simeon blessed them, as a private man and as one of the people, than that he did so in a public character: for, as we have already said, we nowhere read that he was a priest. But there would be no absurdity in saying, that he prayed for the prosperity and advancement of Christ's kingdom: for in the book of Psalms the Spirit prescribes such a eulogia,--a blessing of this nature to all the godly.

"Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord; we have blessed you in the name of the Lords"
(Psalm 118:26.)

Lo, this has been set This discourse was, no doubt, directly addressed by Simeon to Mary; but it has a general reference to all the godly. The holy virgin needed this admonition, that she might not (as usually happens) be lifted up by prosperous beginnings, so as to be less prepared for enduring afflictive events. But she needed it on another account, that she might not expect Christ to be received by the people with universal applause, but that her mind, on the contrary, might be fortified by unshaken courage against all hostile attacks. It was the design, at the same time, of the Spirit of God, to lay down a general instruction for all the godly. When they see the world opposing Christ with wicked obstinacy, they must be prepared to meet that opposition, and to contend against it undismayed. The unbelief of the world is--we know it--a great and serious hinderance; but it must be conquered, if we wish to believe in Christ. There never was a state of human society so happily constituted, that the greater part followed Christ. Those who will enlist in the cause of Christ must learn this as one of their earliest lessons, and must "put on" this "armor," (Ephesians 6:11,) that they may be steadfast in believing on him.

It was by far the heaviest temptation, that Christ was not acknowledged by his own countrymen, and was even ignominiously rejected by that nation, which boasted that it was the Church of God; and, particularly, that the priests and scribes, who held in their hands the government of the Church, were his most determined enemies. For who would have thought, that he was the King of those, who not only rejected him, but treated him with such contempt and outrage?

We see, then, that a good purpose was served by Simeon's prediction, that Christ was set for the ruin of many in Israel The meaning is, that he was divinely appointed to cast down and destroy many. But it must be observed, that the ruin of unbelievers results from their striking against him. This is immediately afterwards expressed, when Simeon says that Christ is a sign, which is spoken against Because unbelievers are rebels against Christ, they clash themselves against him, and hence comes their ruin This metaphor is taken from a mark shot at by archers, [200] as if Simeon had said, Hence we perceive the malice of men, and even the depravity of the whole human race, that all, as if they had made a conspiracy, rise in murmurs and rebellion against the Son of God. The world would not display such harmony in opposing the Gospel, if there were not a natural enmity between the Son of God and those men. The ambition or fury of the enemies of the Gospel carries them in various directions, faction splits them into various sects, and a wide variety of superstitions distinguishes idolaters from each other. But while they thus differ among themselves, they all agree in this, to oppose the Son of God. It has been justly observed, that the opposition everywhere made to Christ is too plain an evidence of human depravity. That the world should thus rise against its Creator is a monstrous sight. But Scripture predicted that this would happen, and the reason is very apparent, that men who have once been alienated from God by sin, always fly from him. Instances of this kind, therefore, ought not to take us by surprise; but, on the contrary, our faith, provided with this armor, ought to be prepared to fight with the contradiction of the world.

As God has now gathered an Israel to himself from the whole world, and there is no longer a distinction between the Jew and the Greek, the same thing must now happen as, we learn, happened before. Isaiah had said of his own age,

"The Lord will be for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offense, to both the houses of Israel," (Isaiah 8:14.)

From that time, the Jews hardly ever ceased to dash themselves against God, but the rudest shock was against Christ. The same madness is now imitated by those who call themselves Christians; and even those, who lay haughty claims to the first rank in the Church, frequently employ all the power which they possess in oppressing Christ. But let us remember, all that they gain is, to be at length crushed and "broken in pieces," (Isaiah 8:9.)

Under the word ruin the Spirit denounces the punishment of unbelievers, and thus warns us to keep at the greatest possible distance from them; lest, by associating with them, we become involved in the same destruction. And Christ is not the less worthy of esteem, because, when he appears, many are ruined: for the "savor" of the Gospel is not less "sweet" and delightful to God, (2 Corinthians 2:15,16,) though it is destructive to the ungodly world. Does any one inquire, how Christ occasions the ruin of unbelievers, who without him were already lost? The reply is easy. Those who voluntarily deprive themselves of the salvation which God has offered to them, perish twice. Ruin implies the double punishment which awaits all unbelievers, after that they have knowingly and wilfully opposed the Son of God.

And for the resurrection This consolation is presented as a contrast with the former clause, to make it less painful to our feelings: for, if nothing else were added, it would be melancholy to hear, that Christ is "a stone of stumbling," which will break and crush, by its hardness, a great part of men. Scripture therefore reminds us of his office, which is entirely different: for the salvation of men, which is founded on it, is secure; as Isaiah also says, "Sanctify the Lord of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread; and he shall be for a sanctuary," or fortress of defense, (Isaiah 8:13,14.) And Peter speaks more clearly:

"To whom coming, as unto a living stone, disallowed indeed of men, but chosen of God and precious, ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house. Wherefore also it is contained in Scripture, Behold, I lay in Zion the head-stone of the corner, elect, precious, and he that believeth in him shall not be confounded. Unto you, therefore, which believe, he is precious: but unto them who are disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed, the same is made the head of the corner," (1 Peter 2:4-7; Isaiah 28:16.)

That we may not be terrified by the designation bestowed on Christ, "a stone of stumbling," let it be instantly recollected, on the other hand, that he is likewise called the "corner-stone," on which rests the salvation of all the godly. [201]

Let it be also taken into account, that the former is accidental, while the latter is properly and strictly his office. Besides, it deserves our notice, that Christ is not only called the support, but the resurrection of the godly: for the condition of men is not one in which it is safe for them to remain. They must rise from death, before they begin to live.

35. But also a sword shall pierce thy own soul This warning must have contributed greatly to fortify the mind of the holy virgin, and to prevent her from being overwhelmed with grief, when she came to those distressing struggles, which she had to undergo. Though her faith was agitated and tormented by various temptations, yet her sorest battle was with the cross: for Christ might appear to be utterly destroyed. She was not overwhelmed with grief; but it would have required a heart of stone not to be deeply wounded: for the patience of the saints differs widely from stupidity.

That the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed There are some who connect this clause with a part of the former verse, that Christ is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many in Israel; and who include in a parenthesis what we have just now explained about the sword: but it is better, I think, to refer it to the whole passage. The particle that, hopos an, in this passage, does not strictly denote a cause, but merely a consequence. When the light of the Gospel arises, and persecutions immediately spring up, there is, at the same time, a disclosure of affections of the heart, which had been hitherto concealed: for the lurking-places of human dissimulation are so deep, that they easily remain hidden till Christ comes. [202] But Christ, by his light, discloses every artifice, and unmasks hypocrisy; and to him is properly ascribed the office of laying open the secrets of the heart. But when the cross is added to doctrine it tries the hearts more to the quick. For those who have embraced Christ by outward profession, often shrink from bearing the cross, and, when they see the Church exposed to numerous calamities, easily desert their post.

36. And there was Anna, a prophetess Luke mentions not more than two persons who received Christ; and this is intended to teach us, that whatever belongs to God, however small it may be, ought to be preferred by us to the whole world. The scribes and priests, no doubt, were then surrounded by great splendor; but, as the Spirit of God, whose presence was not at all enjoyed by those rulers, [203] dwelt in Simeon and Anna, those two persons are entitled to greater reverence than an immense multitude of those whose pride is swelled by nothing but empty titles. For this reason, the historian mentions Anna's age, gives her the designation of prophetess, and, thirdly, bears a remarkable testimony to her piety, and to the holiness and chastity of her life. These are the qualities that justly give to men weight and estimation. And certainly none are led astray by the dazzling and empty magnificence of outward show, but those who are drawn, by the vanity of their own minds, to take pleasure in being deceived.

She had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity This is intended to inform us, that she was a widow in the very prime of life. She had married young, and shortly afterwards lost her husband; and the circumstance of her not entering into a second marriage while she was in the rigor of her bodily frame, [204] is mentioned with the view of heightening the commendation of her chastity. What follows, that she was a widow of about eighty-four years, may be explained in two ways. Either that time had passed in her unmarried state, [205] or it was the whole period of her life. If you reckon the eighty-four years as the time of her widowhood, it will follow that she was more than a hundred years old: but I leave that matter doubtful. The Spirit of prophecy still shone in a very few, who served as tokens to attest the doctrine of the Law and the Jewish religion, till the coming of Christ. In a state of society so dissolute, the elect of God needed such aids to prevent them from being carried away.

37. She departed not from the temple This is a hyperbolical expression; but the meaning is plain, that Anna was almost constantly in the temple. Luke adds, that she worshipped God with fastings and prayers day and night Hence we infer, that she did not visit the temple for the mere purpose of performing the outward service, but that she added to it the other exercises of piety. It deserves our attention, that the same rule is not enjoined on all, and that all ought not to be led indiscriminately to copy those performances, which are here commended in a widow. Each person ought to make a judicious inquiry, what belongs to his own calling. Silly ambition has filled the world with apes, from superstitious persons seizing, with more "zeal" than "knowledges" (Romans 10:2,) every thing that they hear praised in the saints: as if the distinction of rank did not render a selection of employments necessary, that each person may answer to his own calling. What is here related of Anna, Paul applies in a particular manner to widows, (1 Timothy 5:5;) so that married people act a foolish part, if they regulate their life by an unsuitable model.

But there still remains another doubt. Luke appears to make fastings a part of divine worship But we must observe, that of the acts which relate to worship, some are simply required, and, as we are accustomed to say, are in themselves necessary; while others are accessory, and have no other design than to aid the former class. Prayers belong strictly to the worship of God. Fasting is a subordinate aid, which is pleasing to God no farther than as it aids the earnestness and fervency of prayer. We must hold by this rule, that the duties of men are to be judged according as they are directed to a proper and lawful end. We must hold, also, by this distinction, that prayers are a direct worship of God; while fastings are a part of worship only on account of their consequences. Nor is there any reason to doubt, that the holy woman employed fastings as an excitement to bewail those calamities of the Church which then existed.

38. Made acknowledgment also to God [206] The holy melody, which proceeded from the lips of Simeon and Anna, is praised by Luke, in order that believers may exhort each other to sing with one mouth the praises of God, and may give mutual replies. When he says, that Anna spake of him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem, he again points out the small number of the godly. For the substance of faith lay in this expectation; and it is evident, that there were few who actually cherished it in their minds.

39. They returned to Galilee The departure to Egypt, I readily acknowledge, came between those events; and the fact mentioned by Luke, that they dwelt in their own city Nazareth, is later, in point of time, than the flight into Egypt, which Matthew relates, (Matthew 2:14.) But if there was no impropriety in one Evangelist leaving out what is related by another, there was nothing to prevent Luke from overleaping the period which he did not intend to mention, and passing at once to the following history. I am very far from agreeing with those who imagine that Joseph and Mary, after having finished the sacrifice of purification, returned to Bethlehem, to live there. Those persons are foolish enough to believe, that Joseph had a settled abode in a place where he was so little known, that he was unable to find a temporary lodging. Nor is it without a good reason that Luke says, with respect both to Joseph and Mary, that Nazareth was their own city We infer from it, that he never was an inhabitant of Bethlehem, though it was the place of his extraction. [207] As to the order of time, I shall presently give a more full explanation.

b99.es:
34. Y Simeón los bendijo. Si limitas esto a José y María, no habrá dificultad. Pero, como Lucas parece incluir a Cristo al mismo tiempo, podría preguntarse: ¿Qué derecho tenía Simeón a asumir el oficio de bendecir a Cristo? "Sin contradicción alguna", dice Pablo, "lo menos es bendecido por lo mayor" (Hebreos 7:7). Además, tiene la apariencia de absurdo que cualquier hombre mortal ofrezca oraciones en nombre del Hijo de Dios. Respondo: El Apóstol no habla allí de toda clase de bendiciones, sino sólo de la bendición sacerdotal; porque, en lo demás, es muy apropiado que los hombres oren unos por otros. Ahora bien, es más probable que Simeón los bendijera, como hombre privado y como uno del pueblo, que lo hiciera en carácter público: porque, como ya hemos dicho, en ninguna parte leemos que fuera sacerdote. Pero no sería absurdo decir que oró por la prosperidad y el avance del reino de Cristo: porque en el libro de los Salmos el Espíritu prescribe tal elogia, una bendición de esta naturaleza para todos los piadosos.

"Bendito el que viene en el nombre del Señor; en el nombre de los Señores os hemos bendecido"
(Salmo 118:26.)

He aquí, esto ha sido establecido. Este discurso, sin duda, fue dirigido directamente por Simeón a María; pero tiene una referencia general a todos los piadosos. La santa virgen necesitaba esta amonestación, para que (como suele suceder) no se enalteciera con comienzos prósperos, de modo que estuviera menos preparada para soportar acontecimientos aflictivos. Pero lo necesitaba por otra razón, para no esperar que Cristo fuera recibido por el pueblo con aplauso universal, sino para que su mente, por el contrario, se fortaleciera con un coraje inquebrantable contra todos los ataques hostiles. Fue el designio, al mismo tiempo, del Espíritu de Dios, establecer una instrucción general para todos los piadosos. Cuando ven que el mundo se opone a Cristo con perversa obstinación, deben estar preparados para enfrentar esa oposición y luchar contra ella sin desmayarse. La incredulidad del mundo es, lo sabemos, un obstáculo grande y grave; pero debemos conquistarlo si queremos creer en Cristo. Nunca hubo un estado de la sociedad humana tan felizmente constituido, que la mayor parte siguiera a Cristo. Aquellos que se alistarán en la causa de Cristo deben aprender esto como una de sus primeras lecciones y deben "ponerse" esta "armadura" (Efesios 6:11) para ser firmes en creer en él.

Fue, con mucho, la tentación más grave, que Cristo no fuera reconocido por sus propios compatriotas, e incluso fue rechazado ignominiosamente por esa nación, que se jactaba de ser la Iglesia de Dios; y, particularmente, que los sacerdotes y escribas, que tenían en sus manos el gobierno de la Iglesia, eran sus enemigos más decididos. ¿Quién hubiera pensado que él era el Rey de aquellos que no sólo lo rechazaron, sino que lo trataron con tanto desprecio e indignación?

Vemos, entonces, que la predicción de Simeón cumplió un buen propósito: que Cristo estaba destinado a la ruina de muchos en Israel. El significado es que fue divinamente designado para derribar y destruir a muchos. Pero debe observarse que la ruina de los incrédulos resulta de su ataque contra él. Esto se expresa inmediatamente después, cuando Simeón dice que Cristo es un signo del que se habla en contra. Porque los incrédulos son rebeldes contra Cristo, chocan contra él, y de ahí viene su ruina. Esta metáfora está tomada de una diana disparada por los arqueros, [200] como si Simeón hubiera dicho: De aquí percibimos la malicia de los hombres, e incluso la depravación de todo el género humano, que todos, como si hubieran conspirado, se levantan en murmullos y rebeliones contra el Hijo de Dios. El mundo no mostraría tal armonía al oponerse al Evangelio, si no hubiera una enemistad natural entre el Hijo de Dios y esos hombres. La ambición o la furia de los enemigos del Evangelio los lleva en diversas direcciones, las facciones los dividen en varias sectas y una amplia variedad de supersticiones distingue a los idólatras entre sí. Pero aunque difieren entre sí, todos coinciden en oponerse al Hijo de Dios. Se ha observado con razón que la oposición que en todas partes se hace a Cristo es una evidencia demasiado clara de la depravación humana. Que el mundo se levante así contra su Creador es un espectáculo monstruoso. Pero las Escrituras predijeron que esto sucedería, y la razón es muy evidente: los hombres que una vez han sido alejados de Dios por el pecado, siempre huyen de él. Por lo tanto, casos de este tipo no deberían tomarnos por sorpresa; pero, por el contrario, nuestra fe, provista de esta armadura, debe estar preparada para luchar contra la contradicción del mundo.

Como Dios ahora ha reunido para sí a un Israel de todo el mundo, y ya no hay distinción entre judíos y griegos, ahora debe suceder lo mismo que, según sabemos, sucedió antes. Isaías había dicho de su propia época:

"El Señor será por piedra de tropiezo y por roca de escándalo para ambas casas de Israel" (Isaías 8:14).

Desde entonces, los judíos casi nunca dejaron de lanzarse contra Dios, pero el choque más duro fue contra Cristo. La misma locura ahora la imitan quienes se dicen cristianos; e incluso aquellos que pretenden altivamente el primer rango en la Iglesia, frecuentemente emplean todo el poder que poseen para oprimir a Cristo. Pero recordemos que todo lo que ganan es ser finalmente aplastados y "rotos en pedazos" (Isaías 8:9).

Bajo la palabra ruina, el Espíritu denuncia el castigo de los incrédulos y, por lo tanto, nos advierte que nos mantengamos a la mayor distancia posible de ellos; no sea que, al asociarnos con ellos, quedemos envueltos en la misma destrucción. Y Cristo no es menos digno de estima porque, cuando aparece, muchos quedan arruinados: porque el "olor" del Evangelio no es menos "dulce" y deleitable para Dios (2 Corintios 2:15,16), aunque es destructivo para el mundo impío. ¿Alguien pregunta cómo Cristo ocasiona la ruina de los incrédulos, que sin él ya estaban perdidos? La respuesta es fácil. Quienes se privan voluntariamente de la salvación que Dios les ha ofrecido, perecen dos veces. La ruina implica el doble castigo que espera a todos los incrédulos, después de que se han opuesto consciente y voluntariamente al Hijo de Dios.

Y para la resurrección Este consuelo se presenta en contraste con la cláusula anterior, para hacerlo menos doloroso para nuestros sentimientos: porque, si no se agregara nada más, sería melancólico escuchar que Cristo es "una piedra de tropiezo", que quebrantará y aplastará, por su dureza, a gran parte de los hombres. Por tanto, la Escritura nos recuerda su oficio, que es completamente diferente: porque la salvación de los hombres, que se basa en él, es segura; como también dice Isaías: "Santificad al Señor de los ejércitos mismo; y él sea vuestro temor, y él sea vuestro temor; y él será por santuario", o fortaleza de defensa, (Isaías 8:13,14.) Y Pedro habla más claramente:

"Acercándose a los cuales, como piedra viva, desechada ciertamente por los hombres, pero escogida por Dios y preciosa, vosotros también, como piedras vivas, sed edificados como casa espiritual. Por lo cual también está contenido en la Escritura: He aquí, yo pongo en Sion la piedra angular del ángulo, escogida, preciosa, y el que en ella cree no será confundido. Por tanto, para vosotros los que creéis, él es preciosa; pero para los desobedientes, la piedra que los constructores rechazado, éste se convierte en cabeza del ángulo" (1 Pedro 2:4-7; Isaías 28:16.)

Para que no nos aterrorice la designación otorgada a Cristo, "piedra de tropiezo", recordemos al instante, por otra parte, que también se le llama la "piedra angular", sobre la cual descansa la salvación de todos los piadosos. [201]

Tengamos también en cuenta que lo primero es accidental, mientras que lo segundo es propia y estrictamente su oficio. Además, merece nuestra atención que a Cristo no sólo se le llama apoyo, sino también resurrección de los piadosos: porque la condición de los hombres no es una en la que les sea seguro permanecer. Deben resucitar de la muerte antes de comenzar a vivir.

35. Pero también una espada traspasará tu propia alma. Esta advertencia debió contribuir en gran medida a fortalecer la mente de la santa virgen, y a evitar que se abrumara de dolor, cuando llegó a aquellas angustiosas luchas que tuvo que pasar. Aunque su fe estaba agitada y atormentada por varias tentaciones, su batalla más dolorosa fue con la cruz: porque Cristo podría parecer completamente destruido. Ella no estaba abrumada por el dolor; pero habría sido necesario un corazón de piedra para no quedar profundamente herido: porque la paciencia de los santos difiere mucho de la estupidez.

Para que sean revelados los pensamientos de muchos corazones. Hay algunos que conectan esta cláusula con una parte del versículo anterior, que Cristo está destinado a la ruina y la resurrección de muchos en Israel; y que incluyen entre paréntesis lo que acabamos de explicar sobre la espada: pero creo que es mejor referirlo a todo el pasaje. La partícula que, hopos an, en este pasaje, no denota estrictamente una causa, sino simplemente una consecuencia. Cuando surge la luz del Evangelio, e inmediatamente surgen las persecuciones, hay, al mismo tiempo, una revelación de los afectos del corazón, que hasta ahora habían estado ocultos: porque los escondites del disimulo humano son tan profundos que fácilmente permanecen ocultos hasta que venga Cristo. [202] Pero Cristo, con su luz, revela todo artificio y desenmascara la hipocresía; ya él se le atribuye apropiadamente el oficio de revelar los secretos del corazón. Pero cuando se añade la cruz a la doctrina, prueba más los corazones. Porque aquellos que han abrazado a Cristo por profesión exterior, a menudo evitan llevar la cruz y, cuando ven a la Iglesia expuesta a numerosas calamidades, fácilmente abandonan su puesto.

36. Y estaba Ana, una profetisa. Lucas menciona no más de dos personas que recibieron a Cristo; y esto tiene como objetivo enseñarnos que todo lo que pertenece a Dios, por pequeño que sea, debemos preferirlo al mundo entero. Los escribas y sacerdotes, sin duda, estuvieron entonces rodeados de gran esplendor; pero, como el Espíritu de Dios, cuya presencia no disfrutaban en absoluto esos gobernantes, [203] habitaba en Simeón y Ana, esas dos personas tienen derecho a mayor reverencia que una inmensa multitud de aquellos cuyo orgullo no está hinchado más que por títulos vacíos. Por esta razón, el historiador menciona la edad de Ana, le da el título de profetisa y, en tercer lugar, da un testimonio notable de su piedad y de la santidad y castidad de su vida. Éstas son las cualidades que justamente dan peso y estimación a los hombres. Y ciertamente nadie se desvía por la magnificencia deslumbrante y vacía de la apariencia exterior, sino aquellos que, por la vanidad de sus propias mentes, se sienten atraídos por el placer de ser engañados.

Había vivido con su marido siete años desde su virginidad. Esto pretende informarnos que era viuda en la flor de la vida. Se casó joven y poco después perdió a su marido; y la circunstancia de que ella no contrajo un segundo matrimonio mientras estaba en el rigor de su estructura corporal, [204] se menciona con el fin de realzar el elogio de su castidad. Lo que sigue, que ella era viuda durante unos ochenta y cuatro años, puede explicarse de dos maneras. O ese tiempo había transcurrido en su estado de soltería, [205] o era todo el período de su vida. Si se cuentan los ochenta y cuatro años como el tiempo de su viudez, se deduce que tenía más de cien años: pero dejo esa cuestión en duda. El Espíritu de profecía aún brillaba en muy pocos, que sirvieron de señales para dar fe de la doctrina de la Ley y de la religión judía, hasta la venida de Cristo. En un estado de sociedad tan disoluto, los elegidos de Dios necesitaban tales ayudas para evitar que se dejaran llevar.

37. Ella no se apartó del templo. Esta es una expresión hiperbólica; pero el significado es claro: Anna estaba casi constantemente en el templo. Lucas agrega que ella adoraba a Dios con ayunos y oraciones día y noche. De ahí inferimos que ella no visitó el templo con el mero propósito de realizar el servicio externo, sino que agregó otros ejercicios de piedad. Merece nuestra atención que no se impone la misma regla a todos, y que no todos deben ser inducidos indiscriminadamente a copiar aquellas actuaciones que aquí se recomiendan en una viuda. Cada uno debe hacer una investigación juiciosa sobre lo que pertenece a su propia vocación. La tonta ambición ha llenado el mundo de simios, de personas supersticiosas que se apoderan, con más "celo" que "conocimientos" (Romanos 10:2), de todo lo que escuchan alabado en los santos: como si la distinción de rango no hiciera necesaria una selección de empleos, para que cada persona pueda responder a su propia vocación. Lo que aquí se relata de Anna, Pablo lo aplica de manera particular a las viudas (1 Timoteo 5:5;) de modo que las personas casadas actúen como una tontería, si regulan su vida según un modelo inadecuado.

Pero aún queda otra duda. Lucas parece hacer que los ayunos sean parte del culto divino. Pero debemos observar que, de los actos que se relacionan con el culto, algunos son simplemente requeridos y, como estamos acostumbrados a decir, son en sí mismos necesarios; mientras que otros son accesorios y no tienen otro propósito que ayudar a la primera clase. Las oraciones pertenecen estrictamente a la adoración de Dios. El ayuno es una ayuda subordinada, que agrada a Dios sólo porque ayuda a la seriedad y el fervor de la oración. Debemos sostener, según esta regla, que los deberes de los hombres deben juzgarse según estén dirigidos a un fin adecuado y legítimo. Debemos sostener, también, por esta distinción, que las oraciones son una adoración directa a Dios; mientras que los ayunos son parte del culto sólo por sus consecuencias. Tampoco hay razón para dudar de que la santa mujer empleaba los ayunos como un estímulo para lamentar las calamidades de la Iglesia que entonces existían.

38. También hizo reconocimiento a Dios [206] La santa melodía, que salió de los labios de Simeón y Ana, es alabada por Lucas, para que los creyentes puedan exhortarse unos a otros a cantar con una sola boca las alabanzas de Dios, y puedan darse respuestas mutuas. Cuando dice que Ana habló de él a todos los que esperaban la redención en Jerusalén, nuevamente señala el pequeño número de los piadosos. Porque la sustancia de la fe residía en esta expectativa; y es evidente que fueron pocos los que realmente lo guardaron en sus mentes.

39. Regresaron a Galilea. Reconozco fácilmente que la partida a Egipto se produjo entre esos acontecimientos; y el hecho mencionado por Lucas, de que habitaban en su propia ciudad, Nazaret, es posterior, en el tiempo, a la huida a Egipto, que relata Mateo (Mateo 2:14). Pero si no hubo incorrección en que un evangelista omitiera lo que relata otro, no hubo nada que impidiera que Lucas se saltara el período que no tenía intención de mencionar y pasara de inmediato a la siguiente historia. Estoy muy lejos de estar de acuerdo con quienes imaginan que José y María, después de haber terminado el sacrificio de la purificación, regresaron a Belén para vivir allí. Esas personas son lo suficientemente tontas como para creer que José tenía una morada establecida en un lugar donde era tan poco conocido, que no pudo encontrar un alojamiento temporal. Tampoco es sin una buena razón que Lucas dice, con respecto tanto a José como a María, que Nazaret era su propia ciudad. De ello inferimos que nunca fue un habitante de Belén, aunque fue el lugar de su extracción. [207] En cuanto al orden del tiempo, daré a continuación una explicación más completa.

Notas a pie de página:

[199] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur"; -- "alabado también al Señor".

[200] "Ceste facon de parler contient une metaphore prise des arbalestiers, ou autres qui visent au blanc". -- "Esta forma de hablar contiene una metáfora, tomada de los arqueros u otros que apuntan a una marca".

[201] "La maitresse Pierre du coin, sur laquelle est fonde le salut de tous les enfans de Dieu". -- "La piedra angular del ángulo, sobre la cual se fundamenta la salvación de todos los hijos de Dios".

[202] "Extra Cristo"; -- "jusqu'a ce que Jesucristo viene".

[203] La palabra gobernantes (príncipes) parece usarse aquí con sarcasmo; porque su propia traducción es "duquel estoyment du tout destituez les autres, combien que ce fussent les gouverneurs"; - "de los cuales los demás estaban completamente desprovistos, aunque eran gobernantes".

[204] "Quum adhuc vegeto esset corpore".

[205] "Il y avoit tan de temps que son mari estoit mort"; -- "hacía tanto tiempo que su marido había muerto."

[206] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur"; -- "alabado también al Señor".

[207] "Combien que ce fust le pays de ses ancestres"; -- "aunque era el país de sus antepasados".

b100.en:
35. But also a sword shall pierce thy own soul This warning must have contributed greatly to fortify the mind of the holy virgin, and to prevent her from being overwhelmed with grief, when she came to those distressing struggles, which she had to undergo. Though her faith was agitated and tormented by various temptations, yet her sorest battle was with the cross: for Christ might appear to be utterly destroyed. She was not overwhelmed with grief; but it would have required a heart of stone not to be deeply wounded: for the patience of the saints differs widely from stupidity.

That the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed There are some who connect this clause with a part of the former verse, that Christ is set for the ruin and for the resurrection of many in Israel; and who include in a parenthesis what we have just now explained about the sword: but it is better, I think, to refer it to the whole passage. The particle that, hopos an, in this passage, does not strictly denote a cause, but merely a consequence. When the light of the Gospel arises, and persecutions immediately spring up, there is, at the same time, a disclosure of affections of the heart, which had been hitherto concealed: for the lurking-places of human dissimulation are so deep, that they easily remain hidden till Christ comes. [202] But Christ, by his light, discloses every artifice, and unmasks hypocrisy; and to him is properly ascribed the office of laying open the secrets of the heart. But when the cross is added to doctrine it tries the hearts more to the quick. For those who have embraced Christ by outward profession, often shrink from bearing the cross, and, when they see the Church exposed to numerous calamities, easily desert their post.

36. And there was Anna, a prophetess Luke mentions not more than two persons who received Christ; and this is intended to teach us, that whatever belongs to God, however small it may be, ought to be preferred by us to the whole world. The scribes and priests, no doubt, were then surrounded by great splendor; but, as the Spirit of God, whose presence was not at all enjoyed by those rulers, [203] dwelt in Simeon and Anna, those two persons are entitled to greater reverence than an immense multitude of those whose pride is swelled by nothing but empty titles. For this reason, the historian mentions Anna's age, gives her the designation of prophetess, and, thirdly, bears a remarkable testimony to her piety, and to the holiness and chastity of her life. These are the qualities that justly give to men weight and estimation. And certainly none are led astray by the dazzling and empty magnificence of outward show, but those who are drawn, by the vanity of their own minds, to take pleasure in being deceived.

She had lived with her husband seven years from her virginity This is intended to inform us, that she was a widow in the very prime of life. She had married young, and shortly afterwards lost her husband; and the circumstance of her not entering into a second marriage while she was in the rigor of her bodily frame, [204] is mentioned with the view of heightening the commendation of her chastity. What follows, that she was a widow of about eighty-four years, may be explained in two ways. Either that time had passed in her unmarried state, [205] or it was the whole period of her life. If you reckon the eighty-four years as the time of her widowhood, it will follow that she was more than a hundred years old: but I leave that matter doubtful. The Spirit of prophecy still shone in a very few, who served as tokens to attest the doctrine of the Law and the Jewish religion, till the coming of Christ. In a state of society so dissolute, the elect of God needed such aids to prevent them from being carried away.

37. She departed not from the temple This is a hyperbolical expression; but the meaning is plain, that Anna was almost constantly in the temple. Luke adds, that she worshipped God with fastings and prayers day and night Hence we infer, that she did not visit the temple for the mere purpose of performing the outward service, but that she added to it the other exercises of piety. It deserves our attention, that the same rule is not enjoined on all, and that all ought not to be led indiscriminately to copy those performances, which are here commended in a widow. Each person ought to make a judicious inquiry, what belongs to his own calling. Silly ambition has filled the world with apes, from superstitious persons seizing, with more "zeal" than "knowledges" (Romans 10:2,) every thing that they hear praised in the saints: as if the distinction of rank did not render a selection of employments necessary, that each person may answer to his own calling. What is here related of Anna, Paul applies in a particular manner to widows, (1 Timothy 5:5;) so that married people act a foolish part, if they regulate their life by an unsuitable model.

But there still remains another doubt. Luke appears to make fastings a part of divine worship But we must observe, that of the acts which relate to worship, some are simply required, and, as we are accustomed to say, are in themselves necessary; while others are accessory, and have no other design than to aid the former class. Prayers belong strictly to the worship of God. Fasting is a subordinate aid, which is pleasing to God no farther than as it aids the earnestness and fervency of prayer. We must hold by this rule, that the duties of men are to be judged according as they are directed to a proper and lawful end. We must hold, also, by this distinction, that prayers are a direct worship of God; while fastings are a part of worship only on account of their consequences. Nor is there any reason to doubt, that the holy woman employed fastings as an excitement to bewail those calamities of the Church which then existed.

38. Made acknowledgment also to God [206] The holy melody, which proceeded from the lips of Simeon and Anna, is praised by Luke, in order that believers may exhort each other to sing with one mouth the praises of God, and may give mutual replies. When he says, that Anna spake of him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem, he again points out the small number of the godly. For the substance of faith lay in this expectation; and it is evident, that there were few who actually cherished it in their minds.

39. They returned to Galilee The departure to Egypt, I readily acknowledge, came between those events; and the fact mentioned by Luke, that they dwelt in their own city Nazareth, is later, in point of time, than the flight into Egypt, which Matthew relates, (Matthew 2:14.) But if there was no impropriety in one Evangelist leaving out what is related by another, there was nothing to prevent Luke from overleaping the period which he did not intend to mention, and passing at once to the following history. I am very far from agreeing with those who imagine that Joseph and Mary, after having finished the sacrifice of purification, returned to Bethlehem, to live there. Those persons are foolish enough to believe, that Joseph had a settled abode in a place where he was so little known, that he was unable to find a temporary lodging. Nor is it without a good reason that Luke says, with respect both to Joseph and Mary, that Nazareth was their own city We infer from it, that he never was an inhabitant of Bethlehem, though it was the place of his extraction. [207] As to the order of time, I shall presently give a more full explanation.

Footnotes:

[199] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur;" -- "praised also the Lord."

[200] "Ceste facon de parler contient une metaphore prise des arbalestiers, ou autres qui visent au blanc." -- "This way of speaking contains a metaphor, taken from archers, or others who aim at a mark."

[201] "La maitresse Pierre du coin, sur laquelle est fonde le salut de tous les enfans de Dieu." -- "The head-stone of the corner, on which is founded the salvation of all the children of God."

[202] "Extra Christum;" -- "jusqu'a ce que Jesus Christ viene."

[203] The word rulers (principes) appears to be here used sarcastically; for his own translation is," duquel estoyent du tout destituez les autres, combien que ce fussent les gouverneurs;" -- "of which the others were entirely destitute, though they were rulers."

[204] "Quum adhuc vegeto esset corpore."

[205] "Il y avoit tant de temps que son mari estoit mort;" -- "it was so long since her husband died."

[206] "Louoit aussi le Seigneur;" -- "praised also the Lord."

[207] "Combien que ce fust le pays de ses ancestres;" -- "though it was the country of his ancestors."
